title: Well-Formed Formula
body:
A **well-formed formula** is a string the syntax of the language actually permits. The rules
are recursive, building complex formulas from simpler ones:

```
1. any sentence letter (P, Q, R, ...) is a WFF
2. if φ is a WFF, so is ¬φ
3. if φ and ψ are WFFs, so are (φ∧ψ), (φ∨ψ), (φ→ψ), (φ↔ψ)
4. nothing else is a WFF
```

```
(P → (Q ∧ R))     well formed
P ∧ ∨ Q           not well formed: ∧ needs a formula on each side
P → Q → R         not well formed without brackets: the grouping is undetermined
```

Clause 4 is what makes the definition useful, since it is what allows a proof that every WFF
has some property, by induction over the way it was built. That is structural induction, the
same technique [[Proof By Induction]] uses on numbers.

The bracket requirement exists because `P → Q → R` has two readings that differ in truth value,
which is [[Ambiguity]] appearing in a formal language and being ruled out by syntax.
